MINUTES

  COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND TELECONFERENCED

The f0110wing meeting was held in a hybrid format that allowed members 0f the public t0
participate iii—person and remotely via Zoom.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Peak called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Skylar Peak, Vice Chair Drew Leonard and Commissioners Marni
  Kamins, John G. Mazza, and Elizabeth Riddick

  ALSO PRESENT: Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Kellan Martz, Assistant
  City Attorney; Tyler Eaton, Principal Planner; Rick Casswell, Contract Planner; Larbi
  Azzaz, Assistant Planner; Parker Davis. Media Technician; Gail Duncan, Administrative
  Assistant and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Ian Roven led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Chair Peak seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda, continuing Item Nos. 5.A. and 5.C.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on May 9, 2025. The amended agenda was properly posted on May 15, 2025 and the second
  amended agenda was posted on May 16, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Anne noted that speaker slips were a public record and the only requirement was to
  write a name, which could be fictitious, and the item number one wished to speak
  on. Anne raised concerns about potential Brown Act issues at the last City Council
  meeting and for the May 21, 2025 Adjourned Regular City Council meeting due to
  severe technical difficulties. She noted a social media post had incorrectly
  announced the meeting had been cancelled and cautioned that driving without a
  front license plate in Malibu could result in a ticket.

  Tim Barash (with time donated by Joseph Lezama and William Franklin) stated he
  drove to City Hall to present for Item No. 5.A. The California Coastal Commission
  provided late comments regarding their single-family residence after members of
  the applicant team were already in transit and after years ofeffort and neighborhood
  engagement. He expressed the hope that the Commission would support him
  moving forward with the home at the June 2, 2025 meeting.

  Commissioner Mazza noted he and former Commissioner Hill both recommended
  consulting with neighboring property owners as early in the development process
  as possible to avoid appeals during the April 15, 2024 meeting. At that meeting a
  house on Heathercliff was approved. which was later appealed to City Council. He
  noted that neighbors often did not realize the full impact of a development until
  story poles were in place, which was often late in the process.

  Commissioner Kamins thanked Commissioner Mazza for his thorough reviews of
  agendized items.

  Commissioner Leonard toured the Fire Rebuild Center a couple ofweeks ago and
  informed those impacted by the fires that plenty of planners were available to
  provide assistance. He commended the Rebuild Center staff on their reported
  progress to date.

  Planning Director Report

  Interim Planning Director Tamuri provided an update on fire rebuild statistics and
  contact information for both the Rebuild Center and for those impacted by the
  Woolsey Fire.

  Recording Secretaiy Evans reported that the Joint City Council/Commission
  meeting originally scheduled for May 21 . 2025 would be rescheduled to a later date.

  She informed the public that in-person participation in City Council and Planning
  Commission meetings was strongly encouraged as meetings would not be
  continued or cancelled if technical difflculties impacted the ability to accept public
  comment over Zoom. The City would continue to allow remote participation
  whenever technically possible.

RECESS  Chair Peak called a recess at 7:32 p.m. The meeting resumed at 7:38 p.m. with all
  Commissioners present.

  As there were no other speakers present. Chair Peak closed the public comment
  portion ofthe public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

RECESS  Chair Peak called a recess at 8:47 p.m. The meeting resumed at 9:02 p.m. with all

MOTION  Chair Peak moved and Vice Chair Leonard seconded a motion to adopt Planning
  Commission Resolution No. 25—48, as amended, l) replacing Community
  Commercial (CC) with Community-Visitor 2 (CV-2) in the title and Section 3,
  Findings l, 2. 8 and 10; 2) adding Condition No. 15 to state, “Adequate staff shall
  be provided to ensure that traffic does not back up onto Pacific Coast Highway”;
  3) adding Condition No. 16 to state, “All employees and independent contractors
  are prohibited to park offsite in Malibu while working on the property”; 4) adding
  Condition No. 26 to state, “Applicant/owner must submit all required permits or
  certifications for the food truck to the City.”; 5) adding Condition No. 27 to state.
  “Only one food truck shall be used on the
  premises”; 6) adding Condition No. 21
  to state, “The public restaurant is limited to 636 square foot service area used for
  the consumption of food and beverages unless additional parking spaces can be
  provided at which time a Conditional Use Permit Amendment may be requested to
  expand the restaurant space”; 7) adding a Waste Management subheading and
  Condition No. 22 to state, “Trash container areas must have drainage from
  adjoining roofs and pavement diverted around the area”; 8) adding Condition No.
  23 to state, “Trash container areas must be screened or walled to prevent off—site
  transport of trash”; 9) adding Condition No. 17 to state, “The property owner /
  operator shall adhere to a “good neighbor” policy. meaning that the operator and
  employees must respect the rights of neighboring properties. and to the best of their
  ability, shall ensure their patrons’ compliance with the City’s noise and smoking
  regulations and all conditions of approval for the subject use relating to parking,
  smoking. litter, noise, loitering, etc”; 10) adding Condition No. 18 to state, “Noise
  emanating from the premises shall not be audible at a distance of five feet of any
  residential unit between the hours of 10:00 P.M. and 7:00 A.M.. as required by
  MMC Section 8.24.050(L).”; 1 1) adding Condition No. 28 to state. “The Planning
  Director shall have the ability to lower the approved sound level if verified
  complaints are received”; 12) adding Condition No. 29 to state, “The operator shall
  cease the use of the amplified music/sound system upon notice by the Planning
